headline: GOLD STAGES FIRST RECOVERY IN SIX SESSIONS: $4,091 as FOMC Week Opens — Silver +0.79%, Markets Await Warsh's June 17 Debut
snippet: Gold bounced 0.48% to $4,091.62 on June 11 as markets entered the pivotal FOMC week culminating in Kevin Warsh's first press conference and dot-plot release on June 16–17 — the first green session after six consecutive down days that pushed the metal from $5,589 to a 2026 low near $4,074. The June 10 CPI print (4.2% YoY, two-thirds driven by Iran-conflict energy costs) had kept prior sessions under pressure, but the absence of further upside surprises allowed safe-haven buying to reassert; silver recovered 0.79% to $63.90 as Asian physical demand continued to partially absorb Western paper selling. The key binary for gold investors: if Warsh signals a data-dependent one-and-done rather than a tightening cycle on June 17, the rate-hike thesis suppressing bullion collapses against institutional year-end targets that still sit 25–44% above current levels.

headline: ENERGY FUELS TO HIT FULL-YEAR URANIUM GUIDANCE BY JUNE 30 — White Mesa Mill at Historic Low $9–12/lb Processing Cost
snippet: Energy Fuels Inc. (NYSE American: UUUU / TSX: EFR) announced June 11 that it expects to produce approximately 1.6 million pounds of finished U₃O₈ by June 30, 2026 — meeting the bottom of its full-year guidance range (1.5–2.5 million pounds) by mid-year, with all of H2 production representing incremental upside to the range. The announcement highlights White Mesa Mill's processing costs running at a historic low of $9–12/lb, with mining and transport costs at Pinyon Plain tracking $23–30/lb, producing all-in costs well below the current uranium spot price near $85/lb. Energy Fuels also continues building its rare earth element separation capabilities alongside uranium operations, with both revenue streams benefiting from the same mill infrastructure — a dual-commodity leverage play at a time when both uranium and REE supply chains are under acute stress.

headline: 600,000-TONNE COPPER DEFICIT DRAGS AFRICA'S FORGOTTEN MINES INTO THE MONEY — DRC AND ZAMBIA PROJECTS RE-RATED
snippet: Mining Weekly's June 11 analysis argues that the 2026 copper supply deficit — projected at 600,000 tonnes by Morgan Stanley, 330,000 tonnes by JPMorgan, and 150,000 tonnes by the ICSG — is now large enough, and structural enough, to make previously sub-economic African copper deposits financially viable for the first time in a decade. Key supply disruptions forcing this reassessment include Freeport-McMoRan's delayed Grasberg restart (now 2028), Chile production shortfalls, and DRC grade declines; smaller projects in Zambia, Botswana, and the DRC's peripheral zones are now being re-evaluated against a deficit that demand from electrification, data centres, and grid buildout will not close with existing mines alone. The structural implication for junior mining investors: copper exploration companies in Southern Africa are transitioning from speculative to strategic assets.

headline: MITHRIL SILVER GOLD DRILLS 7.22 g/t AuEq OVER 7.25m INCLUDING 22.86 g/t AuEq CORE — Copalquin MRE Due Late June
source_name: Small Caps / Mithril Silver and Gold
snippet: Mithril Silver and Gold Limited (ASX: MTH / TSXV: MSG) released June 10 drill results from the El Refugio and La Soledad expansion zones at its Copalquin District project in Durango, Mexico — top intercept: 7.25 metres at 4.01 g/t Au and 225.1 g/t Ag (7.22 g/t AuEq) from 375.70m depth, with a 0.5m high-grade slice at 15.25 g/t Au and 533 g/t Ag (22.86 g/t AuEq), and six sub-parallel mineralized structures confirmed outside the 2021 resource footprint at La Soledad. The company has completed 11,238 of a planned 25,000-metre 2026 district drill program, with an updated NI 43-101 / JORC Mineral Resource Estimate targeted for late June 2026 — a near-term catalyst that could re-rate this dual-listed explorer at a time when high-grade gold-silver Mexican epithermal assets are attracting increasing acquirer interest.

headline: SUN SUMMIT SPUDS 10,000m IN BC'S TOODOGGONE — TWO RIGS ON CREEK AND FINN ZONES, Q1 2027 RESOURCE TARGETED
source_name: Investing News Network / Sun Summit Minerals
snippet: Sun Summit Minerals Corp. (TSXV: SMN) announced June 8 that its fully funded 10,000-metre exploration drill program at the JD Project in BC's Toodoggone Mining District is underway — the largest campaign in the project's history — with two diamond drill rigs active across the Creek and Finn Zones, targeting an inaugural mineral resource estimate in Q1 2027. The JD Project sits within the Toodoggone District alongside the past-producing Kemess mine and Thesis Gold's Lawyers-Ranch system; the best prior JD results include 17.0 metres at 2.31 g/t Au and 113.1 g/t Ag (within which 6.0 metres graded 5.30 g/t Au and 157.9 g/t Ag) — a structurally controlled gold-silver system covering 600+ metres of strike and 350+ metres of vertical extent that has never been drilled to sufficient density to define a compliant resource.

headline: TRUMP TIGHTENS COPPER'S SECTION 232 SHIELD: 85% US-CONTENT THRESHOLD, BROADER DERIVATIVES — NORTH AMERICAN PRODUCERS WIN
snippet: President Trump signed a proclamation on June 1, 2026 (effective June 8) further tightening the Section 232 tariff architecture for copper imports — expanding the 15% tariff category to additional industrial equipment, broadening derivative product coverage, and lowering the U.S.-content threshold from 95% to 85% to qualify for reduced rates. The June update follows the April 6 imposition of a 50% tariff on semi-finished copper imports and 25% on copper-intensive derivatives, creating the most comprehensive domestic copper protection regime in U.S. history; analysts project that the combined tariff framework will structurally redirect copper trade flows toward North American producers and processors, generating a persistent COMEX/LME price premium that benefits Canadian and U.S. miners with domestic production and refining capacity while raising the cost of offshore copper for U.S. manufacturers.

headline: CHINA'S RARE EARTH INDEX HITS 252.4 — DYSPROSIUM +105% YTD, TERBIUM +103%; PHYSICAL ACCESS NOW THE BINDING CONSTRAINT
snippet: China's Rare Earth Price Index (CREI) climbed to 252.4 as of June 5, 2026, with dysprosium metal at USD $930/kg (+105% year-to-date) and terbium metal at USD $4,030/kg (+103% YTD) — an acceleration driven by Beijing's MOFCOM export-licensing regime that is creating 8–10 week approval delays for ex-China shipments, effectively functioning as a partial embargo for just-in-time magnet supply chains. Market participants now describe the key constraint as physical availability rather than price: ex-China spot pricing for heavy rare earths diverges dramatically from Shanghai domestic references, with dysprosium oxide at ~USD $317/kg FOB versus roughly USD $191/kg ex-works China. The structural implication: Western heavy rare earth projects — including ionic-clay deposits in Brazil and conventional hard-rock assets in Canada and Australia — have moved from exploration curiosities to strategic industrial necessities as the gap between Chinese domestic pricing and what non-Chinese buyers actually pay continues to widen.

headline: METALS FOCUS: GOLD BULL MARKET "STILL HAS LEGS" — Q1 MINE SUPPLY FELL 347 TONNES SHORT OF DEMAND
snippet: Research firm Metals Focus, published via GoldSeek, maintains a bullish 2026 gold outlook with a full-year average price target above $4,920/oz despite the June correction — arguing that Q1 2026 data confirms the structural supply-demand imbalance driving the bull run is fully intact: mine production of 884.7 tonnes failed to meet quarterly demand of 1,231 tonnes without recycling 366 tonnes, a 347-tonne structural gap that must be filled by institutional and investment buying at elevated prices. Metals Focus specifically identifies the pipeline of large-scale gold projects as the thinnest in two decades — a function of dwindling reserves, declining ore grades, and years of under-investment in exploration — creating a long-duration supply ceiling that monetary policy changes cannot alter. The current price weakness is characterized as a demand-side repricing event driven by real-yield repricing, not the structural breakdown that would invalidate the multi-year bull case.

headline: SPROTT: URANIUM MID-YEAR MOMENTUM BUILDING — AI DATA CENTRES JOIN REACTORS AS NEW STRUCTURAL DEMAND DRIVER
snippet: Sprott's mid-year uranium update argues that the June 2026 spot price consolidation near $85–86/lb — following a brief early-year spike above $100 — represents a structurally supported floor, citing three demand pillars that did not exist simultaneously during the last uranium bull cycle: global pro-nuclear policy momentum (Japan restarts, France new-build commitment, U.S. SMR funding), Western utility under-contracting for 2028+ delivery that must be corrected in the next 12–18 months, and a new AI data centre demand driver that requires reliable 24/7 baseload power that intermittent renewables cannot provide. Uranium equities have historically experienced sharp re-ratings when spot prices stabilize above the all-in cost of production for Tier 2 and Tier 3 producers — a threshold most analysts estimate at $70–80/lb — with current prices at $85+ already clearing that hurdle for all Western producers, positioning equity valuations as the lagging indicator.

headline: MOGOTES METALS +159% THIS WEEK: FILO SUR COPPER-GOLD DISCOVERY IS ADJACENT TO BHP-LUNDIN'S $25B DEPOSIT
snippet: Mogotes Metals Inc. (TSXV: MOG) was the top-performing Canadian junior mining stock for the week ending June 11, 2026, surging 159% as the market repriced the company's Filo Sur Project in Argentina — located immediately along strike from BHP and Lundin Mining's Filo del Sol deposit, one of the largest copper discoveries of the decade. Mogotes' standout drill hole FS-DDH-016 returned an 86-metre interval from 108 metres depth averaging 0.7% Cu, 0.55 g/t Au, 2.7 g/t Ag, and 169 ppm Mo — a second copper-gold-silver-molybdenum discovery zone in the Vicuña District described by the company as its 'best-ever' results, at shallow depths and with large-tonnage potential directly analogous to the host geology of Filo del Sol's Tier 1-scale resource. The Vicuña District hosts a combined multi-billion-pound copper system that is now being explored on multiple fronts simultaneously.
